name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,363

clue.text: Leicester City footballer starts to make all his runs exceptionally zigzaggy

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each following word is kept

blocks.clueFragment: make all his runs exceptionally zigzaggy
blocks.note: the first letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A winger famous for weaving dribbles is described as making every run in a zigzag.
explanation.walkthrough: Riyad Mahrez played for Leicester City when they won the Premier League in 2016, and the surface describes his dribbling style.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyad Mahrez is an Algerian winger who starred for that English club, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Note the position of Phillips, say, in a depressed state

blocks.note: Captain Mark Phillips, Olympic horseman and first husband of Princess Anne
being down is feeling low

explanation.surface: Someone records where a man called Phillips is, while feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phillips, say' points to a famous bearer of the surname: Mark Phillips, the British equestrian once married to Princess Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something down is to write it down or record it, as when noting where an item sits on a map.

clue.text: Place full of layers?

blocks.note: surface reading: somewhere stacked with strata, like rock or a cake
setter's reading: creatures that lay eggs, birds kept for laying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' suggests sheets or strata; the question mark warns that it means egg-laying birds instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop where poultry roost and lay eggs is literally a building packed with egg-producing birds.

clue.text: Sam, maybe, in book brought up as conciliatory

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is placed inside it, so the actor goes within the book word
in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, that is backwards

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
Sam Neill, the New Zealand actor of Jurassic Park; 'maybe' marks him as one example of a Sam

explanation.surface: Someone named Sam, raised in a book's pages, is described as peacemaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sam, maybe' asks for a famous Sam, here the actor Sam Neill of Jurassic Park; the whole container is then read upwards, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Emollient literally means skin-softening, and figuratively describes words or attitudes meant to soothe and calm a dispute.

clue.text: Delivery not working to stop, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound, so the spelling may be a different word pronounced the same

blocks.note: a machine that is off is not running
to brake is to slow a vehicle to a halt

explanation.surface: A parcel delivery fails to arrive because something has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off break is a ball from a spin bowler that turns from the off side; 'Delivery' is the cricket sense, a ball bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Each ball a cricket bowler sends down is called a delivery, and this spinning ball is one specific kind.

clue.text: Fool you are told is in coat by Welshman moving transport?

indicators.note: something told is spoken aloud, so letters that sound like the phrase stand for it

blocks.note: an animal's fur is its coat
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
the letters U and R said aloud
Evan is a typical Welsh boy's name

explanation.surface: A silly person, wrapped in a coat beside a Welsh friend, is told something about transport.
explanation.walkthrough: Despite 'is in coat', nothing is enclosed: the pieces simply follow one another. The question mark nods to 'moving' meaning house removals, which a British removal lorry handles.
explanation.definitionFit: A large van used by removal firms carries household goods when people move home, so it is transport for moving.

clue.text: Vote against party

blocks.note: the voter is to be on one side: this is the verb of 'be a'
a no is a vote against, so one who votes against is 'a no'

explanation.surface: A call to oppose a political party at the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: To vote against something is to BE A NO; run together, those words form a slangy word for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is informal British slang for a lively celebration or jolly outing, a noisy party.

clue.text: Bring on section of hospital before trouble

blocks.note: the ear, nose and throat department
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A hospital ward comes ahead of some problem, as if causing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or necessarily cause something as a consequence, much as one event brings about another.

clue.text: Important foreign currency on reflection for economist

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the currency's letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a key factor is an important one
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, an important overseas currency is chosen for an economist.
explanation.walkthrough: John Maynard Keynes was the British economist behind Keynesian economics; fitting, as the surface talks of currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Keynes was the hugely influential twentieth-century British thinker on money, employment and government spending.

clue.text: Irregular actor, contemporary of Marvin L, bringing book out

indicators.note: bringing something out takes it away, so that letter is removed from the actor's name

blocks.note: Marlon Brando, written surname then initial in the same style as Lee Marvin's 'Marvin L'
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: An unconventional film star of Lee Marvin's era has a book released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marvin L' sets the pattern of surname plus first initial, so his contemporary Marlon Brando becomes BRANDO M; take out B and RANDOM remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random follows no pattern or regular order, which is exactly what irregular describes.

clue.text: Hear about worker in old city creating offence in schools

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trial word wraps round everything else
the worker sits in the old city, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: a judge will hear or try a case
Ur was the ancient Mesopotamian city
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A court hears about a labourer in an ancient city committing some school-related crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the worker inside the city, then both inside the word for hearing a case. 'Hear' is the judicial sense, as a judge hears or tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Truantry is staying away from school without permission, a classic misdemeanour among pupils.

clue.text: Rota emerging with shift for record producer

indicators.note: a shift moves things about, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new work rota appears with a change of shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rota' and 'shift' suggest work schedules; 'shift' is the anagram signal and 'Rota emerging' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir George Martin produced almost all of the Beatles' recordings, often called the fifth Beatle.

clue.text: Amusing duo's opening turn

indicators.note: a word's opening is its very start, so only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of duo
a roll is a turn, as a roll of dice or a turn over

explanation.surface: A comedy double act's first routine is funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll describes humour that is dry, quaint and quietly comic, which is a kind of amusing.

clue.text: Sum up fantastic times I hope with no end of relish

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is picked out
with no means lacking, so that letter is taken out of the fodder
something fantastic is wildly imagined, so these letters are rearranged freely

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of relish, the one to remove

explanation.surface: Someone sums up wonderful days they hope for, lacking a little enthusiasm at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The H that ends relish comes out of HOPE, leaving TIMES I OPE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to be or give its perfect summary, capturing its essence in brief form.

clue.text: Scrap guard's first patrol in unused land

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter, so only that is taken from the guard

blocks.note: scrap is waste material
the initial of guard
a guard's round is a patrol

explanation.surface: A security guard's opening beat is scrapped on a derelict site.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste ground is a vacant, neglected plot of land left unbuilt and serving no purpose.

clue.text: Dish - what one might have at night with packet, maybe

blocks.clueFragment: what one might have at night
blocks.note: people dream as they sleep
a packet is a packet boat, a ship carrying mail; 'maybe' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A meal one eats in the evening, perhaps from a packet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' seems to be food, and 'packet' and 'night' extend the picture of a ready meal; here a dish is an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms for a strikingly attractive person, an idealised romantic partner.

clue.text: Major health problem producing short protest amid fear

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the protest word loses its final letter
amid means in the middle of, so the protest goes inside the fear word

blocks.note: panic is sudden fear
a demo is a demonstration

explanation.surface: A disease outbreak triggers a brief demonstration amid widespread alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandemic is an epidemic spreading across many countries, a very serious public medical crisis.

clue.text: Covert bargain of yours once

blocks.note: a steal is something bought very cheaply
thy is the old word for your

explanation.surface: A secret discount deal that used to belong to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy action is done quietly and secretly so as not to be noticed, which is what covert means.

clue.text: Temporary resident entertaining man with priest in film

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so the resident word holds the others

blocks.note: a tenant rents rather than owns
he is a man
short for Reverend

explanation.surface: A lodger hosts a man and a clergyman in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Revenant is the 2015 frontier survival movie starring Leonardo DiCaprio, who won an Oscar for it.

clue.text: Tune from a joint in shabby condition

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the joint goes within the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
a neglected thing gathers dust, its shabby state
J is slang for a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: A melody comes from a run-down pub or shabby smoky den.
explanation.walkthrough: A J for a joint, as in a spliff, goes inside DUST after its first letter, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune an instrument or engine is to adjust it, making small changes until it works correctly.

clue.text: Beer principally left by German helplessly drunk

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of beer
L is the abbreviation for left
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German drinker is left completely intoxicated, mostly by beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely intoxicated, so drunk that one is incapable.

clue.text: A country boy taking in a revolutionary religious leader

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the second article sits between country and boy
a revolution turns things round, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the west African nation
taken as written
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rebellious village lad gives shelter to a spiritual figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes the leader, but it reverses A MALI A LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism, a senior religious figure.

clue.text: Popular bar that's seedy boycotting very non-mainstream company

indicators.note: to boycott something is to shun it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable
a dive is a disreputable bar
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A trendy but sleazy bar refuses to deal with an alternative company.
explanation.definitionFit: An indie is an independent record label or film studio, operating outside the big commercial firms.

clue.text: Papers etc covered by some diaries

indicators.note: something covered by other words lies inside them, so the letters run across the fragment

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Newspapers and similar records are reported in some people's private journals.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, broadcasting and similar outlets together are referred to as the press or mass communications.

clue.text: PA touted possibly for knowing the latest

indicators.note: possibly means in one of several possible forms, so the letters can take another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A personal assistant is promoted for being well informed on the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: Being current with recent news or developments means one is fully informed and abreast of events.

clue.text: Arrangement in support of friend largely

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so most but not all of the friend word is used

blocks.note: being for something is supporting it
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A deal arranged mostly to help out a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the layout or organised structure of something, such as a document or a show.

clue.text: Worthless type now working around North

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new arrangement
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the abbreviation

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A useless person is now employed somewhere around the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Twopenny, said 'tuppenny', describes something costing two old British pennies, so cheap and of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth only two pence is trifling and cheap, hence of no real value.

clue.text: Unpleasant moment in confines of study

indicators.note: confines are the boundaries, so just the outermost letters are kept
one thing in another sits inside it, so the moment goes between the kept letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of study
a tick is an instant, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A disagreeable instant spent shut inside a study room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is awkward or difficult, the kind of predicament that is disagreeable to be in.
